chapter_title: The Explanation of the Peace, what it is; the Righ
spiritual_reading:
You have asked about five holy operations. Though they appear among people as small and commonplace, in their origin they are mighty and held in highest esteem, because they are the inner pattern of the Divine Human in combat and restoration. These five operations are the hidden order by which the Divine good enters into conflict with evil, and by which, after victory, it returns into its own heaven with that good made manifest and confirmed.

The first operation is the peace that the higher heavens impart when the Divine good goes forth to meet hell. The whole angelic heaven acts in consort with that going-forth, surrounding it with tranquil confidence, communicating strength, imparting benediction, and fixing it in steadfastness. This is the first peace: not an outward stillness, but the interior assurance that proceeds from heavenly concord when Divine good advances into temptation.

The second operation is the first right hand: the communication of power from Divine wisdom to Divine good for the work of combat. It is the strengthening of ability for action, given from the inmost source that wills salvation, so that the going-forth may be effective in ultimates.

The third operation is the first kiss: the closest conjunction of love, by which Divine wisdom unites itself to Divine good as it departs into the lower degree for trial. All heavenly societies press into that conjunction, because every order of heaven longs to be conjoined with the saving work; and every guardian care, every kinship of kindred goods and truths within the one heavenly household, joins itself to that descent by an affection of love.

The fourth operation is the first salutation: the act of humble acknowledgment when Divine good enters the lower states. It is the bending of the interior in reverence before Divine truth itself, and before all heavenly orders that are one with it, together with the petition that power and protection may accompany the descent, so that the lower conflict may be carried through in Divine order.

The fifth operation is the first laying on of hands: the full investiture of authority and might from Divine wisdom upon Divine good, whereby it is armed for temptation and made strong for spiritual battle. By that investiture it enters the conflict, meets the collective forces of evil and falsity, endures their hostility, and brings the struggle to its completion.

By these five operations Divine good goes forth from heaven against hell, brings the adversary into subjection, and conquers through the very order of heaven acting within it. And by these same five it returns from temptation into the heavenly kingdom that is its own, not as before, but with victory made permanent in the lower degree.

The peace with which it ascends after victory is the peace imparted by the Divine call that proceeds from the inmost Divine, reaching even into the realm of falsity and evil as a rescuing influx. The peace with which it descended and the peace with which it ascends are one and the same in essence: the same Divine assurance, first given for combat and then confirmed as the state of rest that follows it. Therefore the peace now known among the powers of heaven is shaped according to that primordial peace of saving influx.

The second right hand is the power of elevation given from the Divine operation that restores and orders. It is the effective help by which the victorious is lifted out of temptation into higher clarity and freedom. From this mystery arises the honored practice among people of extending the right hand to a companion: an outward act that, in its origin, is the communication of strength and faithful support.

The second kiss is the renewed conjunction of love from the inmost Divine and from Divine wisdom with Divine good after the conflict has been borne. It is the embrace of reunion that follows separation for the sake of salvation. From this also comes the human practice of embracing in affection, whether at departure or at meeting, because it images the mystery of love that conjoins after trial.

The second salutation is the deeper acknowledgment that follows deliverance: reverence rendered to Divine truth and to the whole heaven in its blessed order, when the restoring Divine brings the victorious up from the lowest distress of temptation. From this mystery comes the honoring of companions among people by forms of obeisance, because such acts descend from the spiritual recognition of order and of another’s good.

The second laying on of hands is the conferral of settled authority and confirmed strength after deliverance. When the restoring Divine lifts the victorious out of temptation, it rescues it from the tumult of falsities and the assaults of evils, gives it ease and freedom in the great heavenly societies to which it belongs, and establishes it firmly in the presence of the inmost Divine that rules all things. By this confirmed investiture it becomes able to lead kindred goods and truths in a new state of heaven. From this mystery comes the human practice of laying hands upon another as an enactment of the greater empowering the lesser.

These five mysteries and operations were first in the Divine, and from there they were taught to people, who instituted them among themselves in external forms; but in the beginning they were not in hellish powers, because hell has no such order of peace, conjunction, reverence, or legitimate authority.

Again, when a person is being brought out of the natural life, a manifestation of saving truth and good presents itself before them, and by that presence redemption is effected from falsity and evil into truth and good. This manifestation quiets the person by interior conjunction and by a stilling influx, removing the terrors that arise from hellish persuasions which would destroy the last remains of order in the natural. By the clarity of that presence and by the recognizable form of Divine mercy, the inner affection of the one who is being saved is calmed as they pass out of the natural.

After this, the heavenly power that holds the confirmation of victory communicates strength and assistance, lifting the spirit out of its lowest entanglement, receiving it into a state of love and peace. The saved one then humbly acknowledges the Divine that redeems, and in that acknowledgment is perfected and increased according to heavenly order, being introduced into the society of the living in heaven, among angels and all who are in truths from good and in goods from truths. Then the person receives the mark of victory and the state of glory that belongs to eternal life.

fills.notes: The sentence requires the resumption of the subject of the embracing: after ‘were making to embrace him!’ the text must specify that the Mother of Life (the Divine wisdom conjoining love to the descending Divine good) was doing so, and then extend it to all celestial societies (‘all of them also’).

The clause balances ‘being honoured and …’ and needs a second predicate expressing the outward valuation of the right-hand act among humans as an ultimate image of the spiritual ‘communication of strength and faithful support’. ‘Glorified’ fits the impersonal, cosmological register better than later moralising verbs.

The sequence demands an adverbial qualifier: the salutation is rendered ‘this time’ in a fuller, restored state after deliverance. A simple connective (‘in’) supports the sense ‘in this time’ without importing later framing.

The obeisance is directed ‘to the God of truth and … the blessed aeons’; the spiritual logic requires inclusion of the total heavenly order, so a collective term (‘all’) is demanded before enumerating ‘the blessed aeons’.

The phrase ‘and … the blessed aeons’ needs a preposition indicating location within the Light-realm societies (‘in the blessed aeons’), matching the chapter’s constant ‘in the aeons of light’ diction.

The contrast required is: instituted among humans in external ultimates (‘in forms;’) yet absent ‘at the beginning’ among Darkness-powers. This keeps the oldest-layer emphasis on correspondence: natural enactments are images of prior divine operations, not moral commands.

After ‘she redeems them from the darkness to the light’ the spiritual sense requires the immediate effect of that παρουσία: pacification and removal of terror. This prepares the next sentence (‘This Light Form calms the person…’), avoiding later soteriological rhetoric while keeping the structural sequence: redemption → tranquillisation → protection.

The narrative sequence is: right hand extended → drawn out and received with kiss → soul makes obeisance → then, at that very moment, perfection and increase according to order. The lacuna must mark that transitional instant tied to obeisance, not introduce a new actor or later ecclesial frame.

fills.fill: the ordinance of the living ones
fills.notes: The spiritual sense requires ‘according to heavenly order’ (not a named church rule). In the oldest substrate register this is expressed as an impersonal ‘ordinance’ belonging to the Living (the ordered societies of Light).

After ‘he receives the crown … glory’ the missing element is the victory-investiture in ultimate form. In this chapter the five signs are enacted as ultimates; thus alongside the crown the restored one receives a ‘robe’ (garment) as the correspondence of confirmed truth surrounding good, leading into ‘glory in the life for ever’.

assessment: Most lacunae are minor letter restorations and are secure. The main recoveries are ¶5 #1 (subject resumption for the universal embrace), ¶11 #6 (a second predicate matching the honoured right hand), ¶15 #1 (external ultimates contrasted with Darkness), and ¶20 #1, #10–11, #15 (the exit-sequence of the soul: redemption, pacification, obeisance, perfection according to order, investiture). These are constrained primarily by the chapter’s five-operation pattern and by the inside-to-outside correspondential movement: divine act first, human enactment as image.
